newsitem.title: GUYANA: Guyana's leader to be cremated in hometown.
newsitem.headline: Guyana's leader to be cremated in hometown.

text.p: Guyana's towering leader Cheddi Jagan, whose death this week marked the end of an era in the former British colony, will be cremated in his hometown on Tuesday, authorities said on Friday.
Jagan, a one-time Marxist whose rhetoric had mellowed over the years, died on Thursday in Washington from heart failure. He would have been 79 on March 22.
His body was flown back from U.S. Andrews air base late on Friday for a state welcome at Georgetown's Timehri international airport.

The government confimed that his funeral would take place on Tuesday at his birthplace of Port Mourant, in Corentyne province, 90 miles (145 km) east of Georgetown. According to the East Indian tradition, his body would be cremated.

Thousands of mostly working class people lined the 20-mile (30 km) route from the airport to the capital, waving small black flags and posters of a man whom U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursday described as "a champion of the poor."
The coffin at the back on an open military truck was draped in the Guyanese flag. Jagan's body was to lie in state from Saturday morning at State House, the presidential palace.

Jagan, whose career spanned five decades, died in the last year of his five-year presidential term. Former prime minister and now interim president Samuel Hinds will lead the country until elections are held, probably around October.

The Guyanese leader died a few hours before another historic Caribbean socialist leader, Michael Manley, the former prime prime minister of Jamaica. A fervent advocate of Third World causes like Jagan, Manley died aged 72 from prostate cancer.
